gravel_god_rating.score_note: The first Estonian UCI gravel qualifier sits inside a nearly thirty-year, thousands-strong bike-marathon institution. The format is new; the event culture and operations are not.

logistics.explanation: Tartu, Tallinn, and Riga airports provide options, while official shuttles connect the point-to-point start, finish, and expo; coordination is real but well supported.

length.explanation: The 126 km course is 78.3 miles, inside the published 60–100-mile score-three band.

technicality.explanation: Ninety-three percent off-road includes dirt and grass, but the organizer describes a fast rolling course rather than technical singletrack.

elevation.explanation: About 1,500 m converts to 4,921 ft, squarely inside the 4,000–6,000-foot score-three band.

climate.explanation: Cool September rain can transform grass and dirt sectors; this is a moderate Baltic variable rather than an extreme-climate event.

altitude.explanation: South Estonia's rolling terrain stays far below the altitude thresholds.

adventure.explanation: A point-to-point line from Otepää to Elva across forests, farms, gravel, dirt, and grass gives the race a strong sense of journey.

prestige.explanation: Nearly thirty years of Tartu Bike Marathon history and thousands of annual riders give the new UCI format national significance.

race_quality.explanation: Established shuttle systems, multiple distances, festival infrastructure, and decades of delivery support a professional score.

experience.explanation: The point-to-point format and South Estonian landscape create a memorable day, even if the terrain is more fast than technically exotic.

community.explanation: Few new UCI qualifiers inherit a nearly thirty-year event with thousands of cyclists and a Baltic festival tradition; the top community score is evidence-based.

field_depth.explanation: UCI qualification layered onto a mass event should create strong Baltic and international age-group racing without claiming an elite global field.

value.explanation: Four distances, shuttle support, festival scale, and qualification stakes make a strong package; the cited official page omits the current fee.

expenses.explanation: Estonia is accessible and generally less costly than marquee alpine destinations, while flights and point-to-point transport keep total costs moderate.

course_description.character: A 126 km point-to-point race from Otepää to Elva on 93% off-road terrain, with relentless short rollers rather than long climbs and a mix of gravel, dirt, and grass.
course_description.signature_challenge: Keeping momentum over dozens of short rises and through grass sectors so a fast rolling course does not become 126 km of repeated accelerations.

suffering_zones.label: Otepää rollers
suffering_zones.desc: Short climbs begin accumulating before riders find a stable group.

suffering_zones.label: Grass and dirt
suffering_zones.desc: Surface drag matters more than gradient through the middle of the point-to-point course.

suffering_zones.label: Elva run-in
suffering_zones.desc: The final rolling sectors reward anyone who preserved speed instead of chasing every early rise.
